title: Mother Bats' Hearts Race for Their Own Babies
summary:
A bat colony can have thousands of bats packed together. How does a mother bat find her own baby? Scientists in Japan found a clue in her heartbeat.

At Doshisha University, scientists noticed that when a baby bat, called a pup, wandered off, only its own mother rushed to help. Pups make special calls when they are alone, a bit like a baby crying.

The team recorded the pups' calls. Later, they played the sounds to four mother bats and measured their heartbeats.

The mothers' hearts beat faster when they heard their own pups, but not other bats' pups. Their hearts also sped up for a strange adult male bat. So a faster heartbeat does not show whether a mother feels caring or alarmed.

Still, the scientists think a pup's call quickly gets a mother ready to take care of her baby.
why_it_matters: Just like a parent can pick out their child's voice in a crowd, mother bats know their own babies by sound.
